messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up from today's UX pass on the model catalog compare table. Found a few low-effort fixes that should make the table feel less brittle: column resize affordance, pin wording, badge semantics, and chip keyboard flow. Would love quick takes before I push updated frames.

Sam: Yep saw this too. The divider is draggable but invisible. Users expect a grip. Can we try a visible handle that appears on hover and stays keyboard-focusable? :eyes:

Olivia: I can mock a tiny 6px handle with hover/focus states. Also it should be an explicit target for screen readers so the action is discoverable.

Jordan: Accessibility: when handle is focused support ArrowLeft/ArrowRight to nudge width and expose aria-live or aria-describedby that says "Left/Right to resize column". Also ensure resize doesn't trap focus.

Sasha: Badges: current color mapping is ambiguous. We use green for multiple meanings. Suggest mapping to icon + single-meaning color: green = meets SLO, blue = cached, amber = borderline, red = fails. Icons help scanning.

Aria: Microcopy on pin feels scary. CTA "Pin version" + tooltip "Lock model version for compare" reads like immutability. Recommend CTA "Pin for compare" and tooltip "Keep this version visible in the compare view".

Maya: Good call. Also the pinned state only shows on the row; it disappears in the compare header which makes it easy to miss. Let's show a small pin glyph in the compare header and include tooltip "Pinned: stays in compare".

Sam: Small UX question: should unpin be possible directly from the header? Right now you must open the overflow menu.

Olivia: We should allow a direct toggle in the header for speed. For org-level pinned models (if/when that exists) keep a confirmation modal; for normal pins, quick toggle + undo toast is fine.

Jordan: Another accessibility snag: filter chips collapse into a "More" menu and aren't reachable in linear tab order. Ensure the More button has aria-expanded and that the popover's chips are placed in DOM order when open so screen readers tab into them predictably.

Sasha: Chip ordering: we currently sort by recency which confuses users. Data shows frequency makes more sense. Propose default "most used" and small label "(sorted by usage)" so users know why order changed.

Aria: On narrow view we hide badges entirely which strips key signals. Alternative: show a condensed summary line inside each row like "Lat 12ms • Cost $0.002 • Acc 93%" linking to the full metric panel.

Maya: Implementation snippet idea for the handle (CSS):
```
.compare-col-handle { width: 8px; cursor: col-resize; background: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 40%, rgba(0,0,0,0.06) 50%, transparent 60%); border-radius: 3px; }
.compare-col-handle:focus { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); }
```

Maya: Proposal to move forward (small batch):
1) Add visible hover handle + keyboard nudge/resizer. (Olivia mock)
2) Update badge semantics and add distinct icons. (Sasha token + icon set)
3) Change pin microcopy, add header pin toggle + undo toast. (Aria copy + toast)
4) Make chips tab-reachable and reorder by usage with a microcopy hint. (Jordan spec)

Sam: Timeline ask: can design deliver prototypes by EOW? Want to run a quick usability check next week.

Olivia: I'll drop a Figma frame for the handle and header pin toggle today.

Sasha: I'll ship a color+icon proposal by Thu.

Aria: I'll update the pin copy, tooltips and undo toast text by Fri.

Jordan: I'll write the accessibility spec for the handle and chip behavior by Thu evening.

Maya: Great. I'll collate the mocks/specs into a single PR description once we have artifacts and file a small user-test plan. :rocket:
